plain.li:
[!condolences,sm:any] I have been thinking about what we owe one another, which is everything, and what we owe ourselves, which is less than we think.

The faith asks very little that is hard and a great deal that is tiresome: to get up, to do the work, to be kind when it is not convenient, to be honest when it is expensive. Anyone can do the hard things once. It is the tiresome things, done every day, that make a people.

So I will say it plainly, as it was said to me: do the small things well, and the large things will take care of themselves, or they will not, and either way you will have done the small things well.

[zeal:crank,!condolences,sm:any] They laugh at me here, and I let them, because I know what they do not.

Everything is connected. The well, the weather, the price of salt, the way the {ANIMALS} have been looking at us. You think it is chance. Nothing is chance. Chance is only a word for what you have not yet been told.

I have written it all down, the whole of it, in a book I keep under the floor. When the time comes, and it is coming, people will want to read it. You may have the second copy.

[!condolences,sm:any] You will know by now that we keep to {IDEO}, and you may think it strange, as outsiders do. I will not try to persuade you. A faith is not an argument. It is a way of getting up in the morning.\n\nBut I will tell you what it gives us: a reason to share the last of the bread, a reason to sit up with the sick, a reason to forgive a neighbour who does not deserve it. You may have other reasons. I only hope you have some.

[zeal:crank,!condolences,sm:any] I have counted the days since the last sign, and the days since the sign before that, and the numbers are getting smaller, and nobody will listen.\n\nI do not say the end is coming. I say that something is, and that it is in a hurry, and that it would be good manners to have the house tidy when it arrives.

[condolences,grave,sm:any] I will not tell you that it was meant to be, or that it happened for a reason. I do not know that, and neither does anyone who says it.\n\nWhat I know is this: the ones we lose are not lost to the faith. They are held. And while they are held, the rest of us must hold each other, which is harder, and which is the only work left to do. Do it. Let others do it for you. That is all the comfort I have, and it is enough.

[condolences,grave,c:pious] {DEITY} keeps a place at the table for every one of us, and the place is never given to anyone else.\n\nThat is what I believe, and I tell it to you not to argue but because it has carried me through every grave I have stood beside. Take it, if it helps. Leave it, if it does not. Either way I am thinking of you.

[condolences,grave,c:nature] The land takes back what it lent, and lends it again, in the grass and the trees and the {ANIMALS} on the hill.\n\nNothing of them is gone. It is only no longer in one place. Walk out in the spring and you will meet them everywhere.

[c:pious,!condolences] Every morning I go out before anyone is up and thank {DEITY} for the day, whatever it brings, and every evening I go out again and give thanks for having got through it.

People ask me what I would do if the day brought nothing worth thanking anyone for. I tell them I have not met that day yet, and I am not young.

I do not ask you to believe what I believe. I ask you to try it once: go out before anyone is up, and look at the day, and see if you do not want to thank somebody for it.

[c:pious,zeal:crank,!condolences] I have been told that I talk about the faith too much. I have been told this by people who talk about the weather all day, which changes nothing and has never once forgiven anyone.\n\nSo I will talk about it. We are not here by accident. We are not here for ourselves. Every one of us is borrowed, and the debt will be called in, and when it is, I would like to be found with my accounts in order. I would like the same for you.

[c:pious,!condolences] The preacher here said something at the last gathering that I cannot get out of my head: that a prayer is not a request, it is a way of paying attention.\n\nI used to pray for rain. Now I pray, and then I notice the clouds, and the dry ground, and the neighbour whose well has failed, and I go and help carry water. The rain comes when it comes. The neighbour needs water now.

[c:nature|p:trees,!condolences] The trees here are older than any of us, and they will be here when we are gone, and they do not hold it against us.

We forget that we are guests. We cut and dig and burn as if we owned the place, and the land lets us, for now, the way a patient host lets a rude guest finish the meal. But the meal ends.

Plant something this season. Not for the harvest. Just to say thank you.

[c:nature,zeal:crank,!condolences] I stopped eating anything that had to be killed, then anything that had to be dug up, and now I am considering whether I can in good conscience eat bread, which was once a field of living grass.\n\nPeople tell me I will starve. People told the first one who crossed the sea that they would drown. I am thinner, but I have never felt closer to the {TREE}.

[c:transhuman|p:bodymod,!condolences] The body you were born in is a first draft. Nobody keeps their first draft.\n\nOur people have taken out what did not work and put in what does, and we are stronger for it, and kinder, because a body that does not ache has more patience. I do not say you must do the same. I say that you are allowed to, and that no one who loves you will mind.

[c:transhuman,zeal:crank,!condolences] Flesh is a rumour. I have replaced my left hand and three teeth, and I intend to keep going until nothing of me can rot.\n\nThey say I will lose myself. I say I will find out exactly where myself is, and replace everything around it.

[p:purebody,!condolences] We keep the body as we were given it. No metal, no grafts, no borrowed parts.\n\nYou will say this is foolish when a leg is lost. Perhaps. But a people who will cut themselves to pieces to be stronger will soon forget what they were trying to protect.

[c:raider|p:raiding,!condolences] Our way is not your way, and I will not pretend it is. The strong take, and the weak learn to be strong, and nobody pretends otherwise, which is more honest than most.\n\nBut there is a law even in that: you take from those who can afford the lesson, you keep your word to your own, and you never, ever burn a field you might want to take next year.

[c:martial,!condolences] Every morning we practise the forms, and every morning I am a little less bad at them, and that is the whole of the teaching.\n\nThe blade is not for killing. The blade is for being ready, so that when the bad day comes you do not have to think. The fewer bad days, the better the student. The best of us never draw at all.

[c:proud,!condolences] I say this without malice: our people were made for greater things than most, and we must live up to it.\n\nThat means more is asked of us, not less. More work, more courage, more honesty. A people that thinks itself above others and behaves no better is only a joke, and we will not be a joke.

[c:loyal,!condolences] We owe everything to those who lead us, and they owe everything to us, and that is the bargain that keeps the roof on.\n\nI hear people grumble about orders. Grumble if you must. But follow them, because the day will come when there is no time to explain, and on that day the ones who follow will live.

[c:together,!condolences] Nothing here belongs to one person. The well, the fields, the tools, the stories: all of it is held in common, and all of it is better for it.\n\nYou will say that people are selfish. Of course they are. That is why the sharing must be the rule and not the exception. A rule is a fence that keeps us from our worst selves, and we are all glad of the fence on the bad days.

[c:free,!condolences] Nobody tells anyone here what to believe, or whom to love, or how to spend their days. That is our whole faith, and it is harder than it sounds.\n\nFreedom is not the absence of rules. It is the presence of choice. Every morning each of us must choose to be decent, with no one to make us, and every morning most of us do. That is the miracle.

[c:pain|p:pain,!condolences] Pain is a teacher, the oldest and the most honest. It does not flatter. It does not lie. It tells you exactly where you are.\n\nOutsiders flinch from it. We do not seek it out for its own sake, whatever you may have heard. We simply do not run from it, and so it has less to say to us, and what it says, we hear.

[c:dark|p:dark,!condolences] Light is a loud thing. It shouts at you about colour and distance and how everything looks, and it never stops to listen.\n\nIn the dark you learn to listen. The walls tell you where they creak. The road tells you where it turns. People tell you what they mean, and not only what they say. Put out your lamp tonight, just for a while, and hear what you have been missing.

[c:tunnel,!condolences] Above ground everything changes: the weather, the seasons, the faces at the gate. Below, the stone remembers.\n\nWe dig not because we are hiding, as you think, but because we are listening. The deep places are quiet enough to hear yourself, and when you have heard yourself you are ready to come up and hear others.

[c:guilty,!condolences] We carry what we have done. Every one of us. You carry yours, I am sure, whether you know it or not.\n\nThe difference is that we say it aloud. Every evening, at the fire, one of us says what we did wrong that day, and the rest say nothing, and that is the whole of the rite. It is not comfortable. It is not meant to be. But we sleep, after.

[p:scars,!condolences] Every mark on my skin is a story, and every story is a prayer. The young ones count theirs with pride.\n\nYou hide your scars. We wear ours. Which of us, do you think, is less afraid of what we have survived?

[p:blind,!condolences] Our holiest ones have given up their eyes, and they see more than any of us.\n\nThe eye is a liar. It shows you surfaces and calls them truths. The blind elder at our fire knows when a storm is coming, and who is lying, and what is in your heart before you have finished your greeting.

[c:highlife|p:drugs,light,!condolences] Life is short, and most of it is work, and the rest of it is worrying about work, and I say this is a terrible waste of a perfectly good life.\n\nOur faith is simple: when there is wine, drink it; when there is music, dance; when there is a fool, laugh with him and not at him. Somebody made the grape. Who are we to insult them by leaving it on the vine?

[p:sober,!condolences] Not a drop, not ever. You may think it hard. It is the easiest thing in the world once you stop.\n\nI have watched good people drown in a cup. I have watched them say things that cannot be unsaid and do things that cannot be undone. A clear head is a gift you give to everyone around you, every morning.

[c:cannibal|p:cannibal,!condolences] You will have heard what our people eat, and you will have flinched, as outsiders do. I do not ask you to understand.\n\nWe waste nothing. Not the meat of the hunt, not the hide, not the bone, not the lessons of the dead. What the dead were, they give to the living. Ask yourselves which is the stranger custom: ours, or burying good food in the ground and walking away.

[p:nomeat,!condolences] We eat nothing that had a face. Outsiders think this is a hardship. It is a relief.\n\nThere is a peace that comes from knowing that nothing died for your supper. The {ANIMALS} in the hills do not run from us. Try it for a season. The vegetables will not mind.

[p:fungus,!condolences] The fungus asks for nothing. Not light, not care, not praise. It grows in the dark on what others throw away, and it feeds us.\n\nThere is a lesson in that for anyone with the stomach for it.

[p:insects,!condolences] You call them pests. We call them supper, and teachers, and kin.\n\nThe hive is the oldest town in the world. It has no rich and no poor, no idle and no greedy. Every one of them works for all of them. Can you say as much for your town?

[c:tea,light,!condolences] I am told that some people drink tea for the taste. This is like saying that some people pray for the exercise.\n\nThe leaf is a teacher: patience in the steeping, attention in the pouring, gratitude in the cup. A hasty brew is a hasty life. Put the kettle on, sit down, and do nothing else for the length of one cup. You will be astonished at what you hear.

[c:coffee,light,!condolences] Our faith wakes before anyone else's, and that is the whole point of it.\n\nThe bean is bitter, as truth is bitter, and it makes you sharper, as truth does, and too much of it makes you shake and talk too fast, which is also true of truth. One cup. Then the work. Then perhaps one more.

[c:peace,!condolences] We will not lift a hand against anyone. People call it weakness. I have seen it take more courage than any charge.\n\nWhen raiders come, we open the gate and feed them, and some of them stay, and some of them leave ashamed. It does not always work. Neither does the sword. But only one of them leaves a town full of widows when it fails.

[c:preach|p:preach,zeal:true,!condolences] I would not be a friend to you if I did not tell you what I know to be true. So I will tell you, and then you may do as you like.\n\nThere is more than this. More than the work and the weather and the worry. There is a way to live that makes the work lighter and the weather kinder and the worry smaller, and it is not a secret, and it is not hard, and I would like very much to show it to you, the next time you are passing.

[p:onefaith,zeal:crank,!condolences] There is one truth and we have it. I say this not to boast but to warn you.\n\nI know you keep to other ways. I know they seem good to you. But a road that seems good and leads nowhere is still a road that leads nowhere, and I would be no friend to you if I did not say so, again, at length, as often as it takes.

[c:craft,!condolences] Make something well, and you have prayed. Make something badly and pretend it is good, and you have lied, and the thing will know it.\n\nEvery piece that leaves our hands carries our mark, and so it must be worthy of it. That is the whole of our creed, and it has kept us honest, and it has kept us poor, and we would not change either.

[c:trade,!condolences] A fair deal is a holy thing. Two people come together, each with something the other needs, and each goes away richer. Where else does that happen?\n\nCheat a customer and you have cheated yourself, for you will never sell to them again, and they will tell their friends. Honesty is not only good. It is good business, and good business is a kind of prayer.

[c:herd|p:nomad,!condolences] The herd knows things we have forgotten: when the rain is coming, where the water is, which of us is afraid. Walk with them long enough and you start to know too.\n\nWe do not own the animals. We walk with them, and they let us, and in return we keep the wolves off. That is the oldest bargain in the world, and the best.

[p:nomad,!condolences] We do not stay. A people that stays grows heavy and fearful, and starts building walls, and then the walls own them.\n\nThe road is our home. Every morning a new place, every evening a new fire. You think we have nothing. We have everything that can be carried, and we have the whole world besides.

[c:sea|p:fishing,!condolences] The sea gives and the sea takes, and it does not explain itself. Our faith is to accept both without complaint, and to mend the nets either way.\n\nPeople from inland think the sea is cruel. It is not cruel. It is simply larger than us, and has other things on its mind.

[p:animals,!condolences] The animals are our kin, older than us and wiser in the ways that matter. We do not eat the ones who share our fires, and we bow to the ones who do not.\n\nWhen {ANANIMAL} crosses your path, stop. Let it pass. It was there first.

[p:charity,!condolences] Whatever you have more of than you need is not yours. It is being kept for someone who has less, and you are only minding it.\n\nWe give a tenth of everything at our gate, to anyone who asks, no questions. Some take more than they should. Let them. It is still less than it would cost us to become people who count.

[p:nomining,!condolences] We do not dig. The deep stone is not ours to break.\n\nYou will say there is iron in the hills and silver under the river. There is. Let it stay. The land holds things for reasons of its own, and when you take them, it remembers.

[p:unlearned,!condolences] Too much learning spoils the hands. We know what we need to know: the seasons, the animals, the ways of our people.\n\nYou with your books and your machines know a great deal, and are you happier? I ask it honestly. I think you would sleep better with fewer answers.

[p:nude,!condolences] We go as we were born, and we are not ashamed, and we do not understand why you are.\n\nClothes are a lie we tell each other about what we are. Take them off and everyone is the same: two arms, two legs, a heart. It is very hard to hate someone when you can see they are cold.

[p:hardy,!condolences] Comfort makes you soft, and softness makes you afraid, and fear makes you cruel. So we sleep cold and eat plain and walk in the rain.\n\nYou will laugh. But when the hard winter comes, and it always comes, you will find us singing and yourselves complaining, and you will wonder which of us was the fool.

[p:chaste,!condolences] Desire is a fire, and a fire in the right place warms a home, and in the wrong place burns it down.\n\nWe keep it in its place. You may think us cold. We are not cold. We are careful, and our homes are still standing.

[olde,!condolences,sm:any] Hearken, friend, for I would speak of holy things. We are not set upon this earth for ourselves alone, but each for the other, as the fingers are for the hand.\n\nDo the small things well, and the great things shall take care of themselves. Rise early, labour honestly, deal fairly with thy neighbour, and give to them that lack. This is the whole of the law, and the rest is but commentary.

[olde,c:pious,!condolences] Each morn ere any wake I go forth and give thanks to {DEITY} for the day, whatsoever it bring, and each eve again for that we have come through it.\n\nThou mayst ask what I would do were the day to bring naught worth the thanking. I have not met that day, and I am not young.

[olde,zeal:crank,!condolences,sm:any] They mock me in the square, and I suffer it, for I know what they know not.\n\nThe end cometh, and soon. I have read it in the stars and in the way the miller's dog looketh upon me. Make ready, friend. Make thy peace, and bar thy door, and lay in salt.

[olde,c:nature|p:trees,!condolences] The trees were here ere we came, and shall be here when we are gone, and they bear us no grudge for it.\n\nWe are guests upon this earth, and a guest that taketh more than he needeth is a thief. Plant somewhat this season, not for thy harvest, but for thanks.

[olde,c:martial,!condolences] Each morn we practise the forms, and each morn I am a little less clumsy at them, and that is the whole of the teaching.\n\nThe blade is not for slaying. The blade is for readiness, that when the evil day cometh thou needest not think. The best of us never draw at all.

[olde,p:charity,!condolences] Whatsoever thou hast beyond thy need is not thine own, but kept in trust for them that lack.\n\nWe give a tenth of all at our gate, to any that ask, and ask no questions. Some take more than is meet. Let them. It costeth us less than to become such as count.

[olde,condolences,grave,sm:any] I will not tell thee it was meant, nor that there was a reason in it. I know it not, and neither doth any that saith so.\n\nThis much I know: those we lose are held, and while they are held, we that remain must hold one another, which is the harder task, and the only one left us. Do it, and suffer others to do it for thee.

[u:none,zeal:crank,!condolences,sm:any] i got to tel you sumthing. evrythin is conected. the wel and the wether and the goats. nobody here beleeves me.\n\nbut i kno. i rote it all down. wen the time comes you wil want to read it. i wil keep you a copy
[u:none,c:pious,!condolences] evry morning i go out and say thank you for the day. evry nite i say thank you agen for gettin thru it.\n\nyou shud try it. its free
[u:none,condolences,grave,sm:any] i dont kno why it hapend. nobody does. but they are held sumwhere. thats wot i think

[sv:deep,!condolences,sm:any] Below the hill a thing is sleeping that was old when the hill was young. We do not wake it. We keep it company.\n\nYou will feel it too, if you are quiet. A weight, under the floor of the world. Do not be afraid. It is not hungry. Not yet. Not for you.

[sv:deep,!condolences,sm:any] Words in the wrong order are the right order, heard from below. Listen: the dark is a room. The room is a mouth. The mouth is saying your name, kindly. Answer, and be welcome. Do not answer, and be welcome also.
